outline: The question: how much memory does a 30-qubit state need, and why?
Amplitudes, normalisation and the Born rule: probabilities are squared magnitudes
zero_state and basis_state as plain Vector{ComplexF64}, and why no wrapper struct
Julia is 1-based: the amplitude of |k> lives at psi[k+1]
Check: every state you build has norm 1 to a stated tolerance
units.summary: A qubit state is a vector of complex amplitudes; n qubits need 2^n of them. Build the zero state and basis states, and read probabilities with the Born rule.
units.title: States as vectors

outline: The question: which index holds the amplitude of |10>, and which qubit is 1?
Bit q of the basis index is qubit q; the rightmost character is qubit 0
Diagram: the bit layout of a 3-qubit index, and kron(op_{n-1}, ..., op_0)
Why this order fits Julia's column-major arrays (reshape gives dimension 1 = qubit 0)
Textbooks (Nielsen and Chuang) use the opposite order: translating between them
Check: bitstrings and indices agree with Qiskit's on every basis state of 3 qubits
units.summary: Little-endian qubit order, as in Qiskit: qubit 0 is the least significant bit and the rightmost character of a bitstring. The source of most simulator bugs.
units.title: Which bit is which qubit

outline: The question: what does a gate do to the point that represents a qubit?
Pauli, Hadamard, S, T and sqrt(X) matrices; checking U'U = I
Rotations R_a(theta) = exp(-i theta a/2): the half angle, and why 2 pi gives -I
Diagram: the Bloch sphere with the six cardinal states
bloch_vector from the density matrix; global phase is unobservable
Born-rule sampling, checked against exact probabilities within 5 sigma
units.summary: Single-qubit gates as 2x2 unitaries, rotations with their half angles, the Bloch vector, and sampling measurement outcomes.
units.title: Gates and the Bloch sphere

outline: The question: a 20-qubit full operator has 2^40 entries; how do you apply a gate without it?
apply! by strided pairs of amplitudes and bit masks, in place
full_operator from the definition, and full_operator_kron from textbook Kronecker products
Property tests: the three agree on random unitaries, qubit subsets and states
Measured: allocations and time of apply! against the dense product
units.summary: Three implementations of the same operation: bit manipulation in place, the element-by-element definition, and Kronecker products, with tests that they agree.
units.title: Applying gates without the big matrix

outline: The question: can two players who cannot talk win a game more often by sharing qubits?
Bell and GHZ states from H and CNOT; diagram of the circuit
reduced_density by partial trace, and entropy of one qubit of a Bell pair = 1 bit
CHSH: brute force over all 16 deterministic classical strategies gives 2
Quantum S = 2 sqrt 2 exactly and from shots; the sign pattern must match the angles
units.summary: Bell and GHZ states, reduced density matrices and entanglement entropy, and the CHSH value: 2 for every classical strategy, 2 sqrt 2 for quantum.
units.title: Entanglement and the CHSH game

outline: The question: can you move a qubit's state without moving the qubit?
measure! with collapse and renormalisation; outcome frequencies follow the Born rule
Teleportation circuit (diagram) and its corrections
Fidelity 1 over random messages; outcomes 1/4 each
Control: without the corrections the fidelity drops (measured), so the check can fail
Deferred measurement: the same circuit with controlled gates instead
units.summary: Measurement with collapse, teleporting an unknown state with two classical bits, and the deferred-measurement principle.
units.title: Measurement and teleportation

outline: The question: how do you tell a constant function from a balanced one with a single query?
Phase oracles and phase kickback; diagram of the circuit
Deutsch-Jozsa on all 72 constant or balanced functions on 3 qubits
Bernstein-Vazirani: every hidden string up to n = 5 in one query
units.summary: Phase oracles and the first algorithms that beat classical query counts, checked on every function and every hidden string.
units.title: Oracles: Deutsch-Jozsa and Bernstein-Vazirani

outline: The question: how many oracle calls find one marked item among N?
Oracle and diffuser as two reflections; diagram of the 2-D rotation picture
P(success) = sin^2((2k+1) theta) exactly, n = 2 to 8, M = 1 to 3 marked items
Overshooting: what happens past the optimal number of iterations
units.summary: Amplitude amplification as a rotation in a plane, with the success probability checked against sin^2((2k+1) theta) for every iteration count.
units.title: Grover search

outline: The question: how can n qubits hold a Fourier transform of 2^n numbers?
The QFT circuit (diagram): Hadamards, controlled phases, the final swaps
Check: the circuit's unitary equals the DFT matrix for n up to 7
A radix-2 FFT from scratch as a second, independent reference
The inverse QFT negates the phases; periodic input gives peaks at multiples of N/r
units.summary: The QFT as a circuit of Hadamards, controlled phases and swaps, checked against the DFT matrix and against an FFT you write from scratch.
units.title: The quantum Fourier transform

outline: The question: how do you read off an eigenvalue of a unitary you can only apply?
Controlled U^(2^j) and the inverse QFT; diagram of the circuit
Exact result for dyadic phases; the closed-form distribution otherwise
The best estimate has probability at least 4/pi^2 (checked)
A worked catch: Qiskit's phase_estimation bit-reverses its output register
units.summary: Reading an eigenphase into a register with controlled powers of U and an inverse QFT, checked against the closed-form outcome distribution.
units.title: Phase estimation

outline: The question: how much noise destroys a quantum advantage?
Density matrices and Kraus channels; K dagger, not K transpose
Bloch-vector formulas for depolarising, amplitude damping (T1) and dephasing (T2)
CHSH under depolarising noise: the threshold p = 1 - 1/sqrt 2
Monte Carlo trajectories agree with the density-matrix result within 5 sigma
units.summary: Mixed states, Kraus channels, T1 and T2, and quantum trajectories, with the depolarising level where CHSH stops beating classical.
units.title: Noise and density matrices

outline: The question: how do you compute the gradient of a circuit you can only run?
Expectation values of Pauli strings without forming their matrix
Parameter shift: exact gradients from two shifted runs, against finite differences
VQE reaches E0 = -sqrt 2 on the test Hamiltonian
Control: a product-state ansatz without entanglement stays at -1.25
units.summary: Parameter-shift gradients and a small VQE, checked against finite differences and the exact ground-state energy.
units.title: Variational algorithms

outline: The question: every test passes; how do you know the simulator is right?
Layer 1, redundant implementations; layer 2, closed-form theory checks
Layer 3, an independent reference (Qiskit), compared amplitude by amplitude
Layer 4, controls that must fail; layer 5, mutation testing with 22 injected bugs
Case study: a CHSH sign pattern that gave S = 0
Case study: Qiskit's undocumented bit reversal in phase_estimation
Case study: a measure! flip that survived until a lopsided test was added
units.summary: Five layers of evidence: redundant implementations, theory checks, an independent reference, controls that must fail, and mutation testing, with three real bugs as case studies.
units.title: How you know a result is not wrong
